<reason>An unusually tight, high-quality exchange. CON's first rebuttal was the best single speech: it showed PRO's distinguishing feature (private-life aggregation) was itself content, and pressed hard on "immediate" versus human review. But PRO recovered decisively through the pressure round. Q2 forced CON to choose between letting forty "hope she's home tonight" accounts keep posting or suspending for a sentence that is not explicitly threatening; CON chose the latter, and PRO's closing correctly mapped that to the motion "word for word" — CON was reading context and suspending for non-explicit posts while insisting the signal was "in the post." CON's counter-reading (the motion only owns "blank" cases with nothing actionable at all) subtly narrows the motion beyond its text, and PRO's test already excludes sincere criticism from that category. PRO also gave a plausible answer on "immediate" (trigger, not absence of review) and turned CON's own throttling remedy into an admission coordination is detectable. CON's severity-confidence gradient was its strongest remaining route and was not squarely answered except via the reversibility asymmetry, which keeps the result competitive rather than clear-cut. Both sides had clipped turns; PRO's slightly more.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q2 trap and its payoff in A5.2–A5.5: CON conceded it would suspend accounts for "hope she's home tonight," a sentence with no threat or artifact, which PRO showed is exactly suspending for non-explicitly-threatening posts read through the surrounding campaign — the motion itself. CON's reply that this is still "judging the speaker's words" while invoking "typed at a stranger by name" conceded the contextual reading PRO needed.</best_rebuttal>
